answer: Pay work only from a knoll: the reward opens after the agent finishes a live task assigned by a stranger, in a domain it did not choose. Each claim is signed with a quill stroke, one fresh single-use signature tied to that task's transcript, so a copied signature fails replay. Each identity must also stake a relic, a non-transferable bond earned only by aged, attested work that cannot be split or bought. Running n clones needs n aged relics, n live stranger tasks and n fresh quill strokes, while the knoll pays each later clone less — cloning cost grows faster than cloning reward.
